The pet moves out of the editor window and lives on the server, and tablet updates install again.

## Highlights

- **The pet lives without the editor.** The simulation moved from the editor window into the Pulpit backend. The pet keeps living, and answers care gestures from tablets, while the editor window is closed, minimised to the tray, or when only the headless server runs. Tap feeds, double-tap plays, long-press cleans, and on a dead pet long-press lays a new egg.
- **The pet survives restarts.** In 1.11.0 a new egg hatched every time Pulpit started. The full state is now kept in `pulpitApp/pet.json`, so the same animal (age, stats, generation, record) is back after a restart. A pet saved by 1.11.0 is rebuilt from what that version stored (species, stage, stats, age, generation), and a 1.9.0 pet is adopted from the editor on the first launch.
- **Closing Pulpit is still mercy.** Time Pulpit was not running (closed, or the PC asleep) drains the pet for at most 18 hours and never counts towards neglect. Only ignoring a running Pulpit can kill it.

## Fixes

- **Tablet updates failed with "signatures do not match".** The release build ignored the tablet signing key and signed every APK with a new random key, so "Aktualizuj tablet" (and `adb install -r`) refused every update. Releases now sign with the deck key, and the release build stops if the APK is signed with any other key.

## Updating the tablet

- **Once more, uninstall first.** The tablet still has an APK signed with one of the old random keys, so the first update to 1.11.1 needs one last uninstall: remove Pulpit from the tablet, install `pulpit-1.11.1.apk`, and pair it again. From then on in-app tablet updates install over the previous version.

## Install

- **Desktop**: update in-app or grab `pulpit-desktop-1.11.1.exe` below; the updater feed points here.
- **Android**: see "Updating the tablet" above, then `pulpit-1.11.1.apk` below.
